title: brief-flow-event/v1
description: One brief lifecycle fact, one JSON object per line of a portable JSONL export (spec/brief-flow-event-v1.md). The accounting unit is the brief's stable uuid (the brief-v2 `id:`); pull requests, commits and board rows are evidence about a brief, never a unit of their own. This schema is the SHAPE contract only. The semantic rules a schema cannot express live in the reference validator (statusgen/briefevent.go, ParseBriefEvent): occurrence bounds, receipt-not-before-occurrence, the per-milestone required members, the `must_understand` refusal, the person-identifier refusal and canonical fact digests. Unknown top-level members are allowed so a later optional extension round-trips unchanged through an older reader; an extension a reader MUST understand is named in `must_understand`, and a reader that does not know it refuses the event. A member named like a person identifier (login, name, email, author and similar) is refused at any depth by the validator: actors are recorded as roles only.

schema.description: The event contract and its major version. A reader refuses any other value: a later major version may change a meaning this reader would silently misread.

fact_id.description: The canonical fact id. Use the source's own immutable event id where one exists; otherwise the deterministic legacy derivation (namespace, object, revision, kind and subject hashed under a derivation version). Every observation of one fact carries the same id, so a live capture and a later import resolve to one fact. Same id with the same digest is idempotent; same id with a different digest is a conflict held for inspection, never a second fact.

brief_uuid.description: The brief's stable identity: its brief-v2 `id:` uuid v4. It survives renumber, rename and archive. Never derived from a title or an alias.

alias.description: The `<stream>/<NN>` alias the brief carried when the fact occurred. An alias is effective-dated and may later name a different brief; it is a locator, never an identity.

milestone.description: The fact kind. Producers record facts; whether a fact is a FIRST milestone or a repeated episode is decided by the stage reducer, never by the producer.

occurred_at.description: When the fact happened, as best the source knows it, in UTC. Its quality is stated by `precision` and, when the source only brackets the instant, by `occurred_after`/`occurred_before`.

received_at.description: When this observation was received by the collector, in UTC. Receipt order is not occurrence order.

occurred_after.description: Optional inclusive lower bound on the occurrence instant (UTC).

occurred_before.description: Optional inclusive upper bound on the occurrence instant (UTC).

precision.description: How `occurred_at` was obtained: `event` is the source's own event time; `commit` is a commit-time proxy; `poll` is an observation between two polls; `day` is a date only. Absent means unstated, which ranks below every stated value.

source_authority.description: Which source observed the fact, in precedence order: `forge` (the forge's own event record), `producer` (the acting tool's receipt written after the act succeeded), `git` (main-branch history), `historian` (a live board-historian row), `backfill` (a historian row replayed from git). Absent means unstated, which ranks last.

source_ref.description: The source object this observation read: its kind, its immutable id and the revision read.

coverage.description: Whether the source read behind this observation was complete. `partial` (a truncated page, a missing range) and `unknown` are never read as complete, and missing data is never read as zero activity.

initiator_role.description: The role classification of whoever initiated the act. Role names only; `unknown` is an explicit value, never a default.

executor_role.description: The role classification of whoever executed the act, kept separate from the initiator (a human may ask, a worker may act).

brief_revision.description: The brief's own revision counter (brief-v2 `version:`) in force when the fact occurred.

owner_cell.description: The cell that owned the brief when the fact occurred. Absent means unknown ownership, which stays unknown in grouped reports.

owner_stream.description: The stream that owned the brief when the fact occurred.

visibility.description: Who may read this fact. Absent is treated as `restricted`: nothing is published without an explicit `public`.

contribution.description: The contribution (a pull request) a `pr_*` fact is about.

ref.description: A stable contribution reference, for example `pr:12`.

kind.description: `implementation` delivers the brief; `authoring` only writes or edits the brief and never counts as coded.

draft.description: On `pr_opened`: whether the pull request was created as a draft. A pull request created ready is ready-at-creation; no flip is invented.

replaces.description: On `pr_opened`: the contribution this one replaces. A replaced contribution is superseded, not abandoned.

acceptance.description: The acceptance owner's statement about which contributions the brief needs (`acceptance_scope`) or what a `verified`/`done` fact covered. Only `complete` coverage supports whole-brief completion.

revision.description: The acceptance (brief) revision the statement binds to.

contributions.description: On `acceptance_scope`: every contribution reference the brief's acceptance needs.

status_from.description: On `status_observed`: the previously recorded board status, or empty for a historian seed row. A seed records state; it is never a birth.

alias_reason.description: On `alias_assigned`: why the alias took effect.

supersedes.description: The fact id this fact corrects. On `retraction` the target is withdrawn without replacement.

import_run.description: The import or collection run that produced this observation.

must_understand.description: Member names a reader MUST understand to use this event. A reader that does not know a listed member refuses the event rather than guessing; a member NOT listed here is optional and round-trips unchanged.
